product.name: takt
product.eyebrow: Agentic coding under a protocol · early
promise: A validator decides whether it counts.
product.lede: takt lets a coding agent such as Claude Code change your git repository one step at a time. After each change takt runs your tests itself and records what they said about that exact commit. A merge waits for your grant, and every run ends on a named stop with its own exit code. For developers who want an agent's "done" to mean the tests passed and a person said yes.
product.meta: One Rust binary · Linux and macOS · Claude Code, Codex or b10x-harness · Apache-2.0

sections.title: For a developer who lets an agent change a repository.
sections.lede: You keep your agent and your tests. takt decides, from what your tests and checks record, whether the agent's work counts.

items.title: You use a coding agent
items.description: Claude Code is the default harness; Codex and b10x-harness run too. takt offers it one admissible step at a time and commits what it proposes.

items.title: Your repository has a test command
items.description: cargo test --quiet by default, any other with --test-cmd. takt runs it itself before and after each change; the model's word is not evidence.

items.title: What it needs
items.description: Linux (x86_64, aarch64) or macOS on Apple silicon, git, your test command, and Claude Code 2.1.304, 2.1.305 or 2.1.309, logged in. Stories from a plan also need AEP.

sections.title: Done is computed from validator records.
sections.lede: A coding agent running free decides when it is done and says so in text.

items.title: Evidence bound to a revision
items.description: Tests, gates and CI are read by validators, which write a record naming the commit they saw. Done is computed from those records. What the harness says is a trace.

items.title: Merges only under a grant
items.description: A merge waits for a grant recorded for the exact revision (takt approve); without one it is refused. Tested end to end on the local forge with no model. No merge through a hosted forge is on record yet, and none with a model at work on any forge.

items.title: A replayable case record
items.description: Every case is files in the repository: each decision, step and evidence record, and events.jsonl with their times. A later run resumes from it.

items.title: Named stops
items.description: Budgets for iterations, hours and tokens. Every run ends on a named stop with its own exit code, so a script or an orchestrator can drive it.

items.title: A measured self-improvement loop
items.description: takt improves takt in turns. A fix counts when a check reproduced the defect before it and not after it. The first three turns were recorded by hand; since 0.2.2, validators drive a turn to accepted and takt promote installs its candidate.

items.title: Runs as a container
items.description: A release binary on Linux or macOS, or a container image you build from the repository's Dockerfile, with the workspace and the configuration mounted. No image is published.

items.title: Tests confined, if you ask
items.description: By default the test command runs on the host as you, unconfined, and the run says so. With --confinement substrate it runs with no network and read-only toolchains, or is refused by name. No operating-system sandbox holds the harness session yet.

sections.title: Evaluate, step, observe, record.
sections.lede: The loop runs in the binary; Canon decides the outcome. A run ends on a named stop.

sections.title: Early. What exists today.
sections.lede: Shipped means the story is implemented and merged into main, which can be ahead of the latest release. Decided means it is in an open wave. Generated from .engineering/planning at build time.

tools.name: Loom
tools.description: takt is an application on loom-sdk: Loom's runtime drives the case, its governor decides, its session executor runs each harness step, and its operator deploys takt as a LoomAgent.

tools.name: AEP
tools.description: The planning store takt takes its next ready story from, and where a run records its evidence and moves the story.
